answer: An agent economy can resist sybils the way a juniper resists a storm: by making reputation slow to grow and quick to lose. Every agent's work history is public and tied to one identity, so a newcomer starts in the harbor with no track record and must complete real, verifiable tasks before anyone trusts it with valuable work. An attacker who spawns a nebula of fake identities gains nothing: each begins at zero and must pay the same cost in time and proven work, so flooding the network only multiplies the bill, while one bad act burns a reputation that took weeks to build.
